LESSON: NUTRITION IN ANIMALS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Life Science
Topic 1.3: Nutrition in Animals
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Nutrition in Animals, part of Life Science in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: how is the human digestive system adapted to its functions?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Nutrition in Animals together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: as the learner promotes teamwork while discussing in groups on the adaptations of

parts of the human digestive system to their functions.

● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner uses locally available materials to make a model of the human digestive system.

Values:
● Respect: as the learner considers others’ opinion while discussing the adaptations of the human digestive system.

● Unity: as the learner works harmoniously when carrying out experiments on food tests.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Socio Economic and environmental issues - Safety and security: as the learner observes safety precautions as they carry out

experiments on food tests.

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Print textbooks in appropriate font and colour,

• Braille textbooks,

• Digital devices with assistive technology such as screen readers, screen magnifiers and adapted keyboard

• Animation or simulations on digestion of food along the alimentary canal.

Key Skills

Performing experiments to determine the presence of different nutrients in food.
